statement: An equilateral triangle has an altitude of length $6$. What is the perimeter of the triangle?

choices.misconception: I found the short leg of the 30-60-90 triangle, $2\sqrt{3}$, and used it as a full side of the equilateral triangle, but it is only half of a side.
I multiplied the altitude by $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ instead of dividing by it, so each side came out $3\sqrt{3}$ and the perimeter $9\sqrt{3}$.
I treated the altitude as if it were a side, so I got 3 times 6 = 18.
I thought each side was the altitude times $\sqrt{3}$, so each side was $6\sqrt{3}$ and the perimeter $18\sqrt{3}$.

hints: The altitude splits the equilateral triangle into two 30-60-90 right triangles.
In a 30-60-90 triangle the sides are in the ratio $1 : \sqrt{3} : 2$, and the altitude is the leg opposite the $60^\circ$ angle.
The short leg is $\frac{6}{\sqrt{3}} = 2\sqrt{3}$, which is half of a side, so a full side is $4\sqrt{3}$.

solutions.reliable: The altitude splits the triangle into two $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ triangles. The altitude is the longer leg, so the short leg, which is half of a side, is $\frac{6}{\sqrt{3}} = 2\sqrt{3}$. A full side is $4\sqrt{3}$, and the perimeter is $3 \cdot 4\sqrt{3} = 12\sqrt{3}$.
solutions.elegant: For side $s$, the altitude is $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}s$, so $\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}s = 6$ gives $s = \frac{12}{\sqrt{3}} = 4\sqrt{3}$ and the perimeter is $3s = 12\sqrt{3}$.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
